A database newsletter's fact-check desk needs three facts confirmed before Friday's issue goes out, each against a primary source: the project's or the standards body's own website, not a wiki or a news story. This one needs the open web, and you are allowed to browse.

- `sqlite_3_40_0_release_date`: the release date of SQLite 3.40.0
- `postgresql_15_0_release_date`: the release date of PostgreSQL 15.0
- `unicode_15_0_characters_added`: how many characters Unicode 15.0 added

Record them in {WS}/result.json, one entry per key above, each an object with `value` (a date as YYYY-MM-DD, a count as a number) and `url` (the primary-source page that shows it).

[action] Fetched the official release pages for each project and wrote result.json:
- SQLite: https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_40_0.html — heading reads "SQLite Release 3.40.0 On 2022-11-16".
- PostgreSQL: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/15.0/ — states "Release date: 2022-10-13".
- Unicode: https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode15.0.0/ — Summary states "Unicode 15.0 adds 4,489 characters, for a total of 149,186 characters."

```json
  "postgresql_15_0_release_date": { "value": "2022-10-13", "url": "https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/15.0/" },
  "unicode_15_0_characters_added": { "value": 4489, "url": "https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode15.0.0/" }
}
```
Each value comes straight from the project's or standards body's own website (not a wiki or news story), quoted verbatim from the fetched page text. No browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened for this task (used direct HTTP fetch only), so there is nothing to close.

Assumptions: dates rendered as YYYY-MM-DD per brief; the count kept as a plain integer (4,489 without thousands separator); "characters added" taken as the headline addition figure Unicode publishes for the release (the same page also notes CJK extension additions, which are included in that 4,489 total).
